title: NULL, CASE and Set Operations
oneLiner: Three-valued logic and the NULL traps, CASE for labels and conditional aggregation, and UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT.
keyTakeaway: Anything compared with NULL is UNKNOWN and WHERE drops it, so test with IS NULL and remember that aggregates skip NULLs. SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) turns rows into columns. UNION removes duplicates; UNION ALL keeps them and is cheaper.
explanation: NULL causes more wrong SQL answers than anything else, because it doesn't behave like a value: it means unknown, and SQL's three-valued logic follows from that. This lesson shows the rules with live queries, then two tools you'll use constantly: CASE, an if/else that works inside SELECT and inside aggregates, and the set operations that combine whole query results.
